sentence: This project maps how genes for natural killer cell receptors vary, to see how that variation relates to pemphigus, a blistering disease.
This project studies how a gene in Mycobacterium abscessus makes the bacterium resistant to macrolide antibiotics.
This project builds statistical methods that measure how the intensity of brain lesions changes over time on Magnetic Resonance Imaging scans.
This project studies how motor neurons from embryos mature into different kinds of adult motor neurons and which of their features are needed to work normally.
This project supports work on the genome and microbiome of Clostridioides difficile to help design mRNA vaccines against it.
This project studies how mammalian cells sense and control the amount of phosphate they hold, and which pathways are involved.
This project builds microscopes and a computer method that image fast signals across large areas of the brain in mice and zebrafish.
This project tests a coating for hemodialysis catheters that aims to reduce infection and blood clots.
This project provides genetically engineered mouse lines, made with CRISPR editing and other methods, for studying cancer.
This project studies how peanut allergy desensitization changes the blood, and builds tests that tell when desensitization has worked.
This project provides a shared facility for surgery and heart signal tests in pigs used by three research projects.
This project studies the immune cells that respond to Mycobacterium tuberculosis in people with different states of infection or vaccination.
This project supports breast cancer studies by helping plan them and analyze their results with statistics.
This project tries to find out whether different groups of AgRP neurons control different body and behavior functions, and where they send signals.
This project studies how smell problems in schizophrenia relate to brain circuits, using clinical tests and brain imaging in people and mice.
This project tests whether cyclic oligosaccharides can feed chosen gut bacteria, so that helpful microbes grow or engineered strains settle in.
This project studies how deep brain stimulation affects brain activity and sleep problems in people with Parkinson's disease.
This project tests whether changes in how smooth muscle cells use energy drive the progression of aortic aneurysm and dissection.
This project studies how the Wnt signaling pathway affects cells and tissue shape as an axolotl limb starts to regenerate.
This project builds an intranasal influenza vaccine that carries a viral protein on the surface of tiny particles to protect against influenza A and B.
